key_insight: AgentRVOS reverses the usual pipeline by first building object-centric tracks and then letting a multimodal reasoning agent (MLLM) decide which track matches the language query, enabling better temporal reasoning and spatial coverage without any training.
problem_solved: Existing training-free RVOS pipelines force the MLLM to pick keyframes before object-level evidence exists, hurting temporal consistency and grounding accuracy; this paper addresses zero-shot referring video object segmentation with improved spatio-temporal reasoning and robustness.
method: Extract object-centric tracks from the video using off-the-shelf detectors/trackers to obtain per-track visual evidence across time.
Convert each track into compact multimodal representations (frame crops, embeddings, short captions) and feed them to an agent-style MLLM that reasons over tracks to identify the referred object.
Produce final masks by grounding the chosen track to frames and applying a video segmentation/mask-propagation module—no task-specific training required.
impact: Delivers stronger, more interpretable zero-shot RVOS by shifting reasoning to object-level tracks, improving temporal coverage and accuracy for downstream tasks where training data is limited or unavailable.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram contrasting prior keyframe-first approach vs. AgentRVOS track-first approach (showing reversed order).
Timeline visualization with multiple object tracks (colored ribbons) and the agent selecting the correct track based on the language query.
Before/after example frames: original frames, predicted masks from prior pipeline, and masks from AgentRVOS to highlight improved temporal consistency.
Bar chart or table summarizing zero-shot performance gains and qualitative robustness (e.g., occlusion, fast motion).
paper_title: AgentRVOS: Reasoning over Object Tracks for Zero-Shot Referring Video Object Segmentation
paper_authors: Woojeong Jin, Jaeho Lee, Heeseong Shin, Seungho Jang, Junhwan Heo
